```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
theme(theme_bw())
```
Simulate data following a linear regression model.

Example: the relationship between water temperature and the length of copepods.

1. Choose our parameters
2. Simulate data
3. Fit the model
4. Interpret the model

## Choose parameters

Our model has three parameters: two betas and a sigma. our simulation needs one more parameter, our sample size.

```{r}
beta_0 <- 3000 # intercept: length of a coperpods in um when temp is degC

beta_1 <- -55 # slope: change in length per degC

sigma <- 100 #standard dev of the residuals, the "spread" around the line

n <- 50 # sample size
```
## Simulate the data
1. Simulate the _predictor_
2. Calcualte the _expected_
3. Simulate the _response_
4. Assemble a data 

### Simulate the predictor
```{r}
temp_c <- runif(n, min = 2, max = 14)
```

### Calculate the expected
```{r}
exp_length_um <- beta_0 + beta_2 * temp_c
```

### Simulate the repsonse

The response is normally distributed around the line.

```{r}
length_um <- rnorm(n, mean = exp_length_um, sd = sigma)
# notice the mean is the vector of the expected values
```

### Assemble the dataframe
```{r}
# Create a tibble
copepods <- tibble(temp_c, length_um)

# Visualize
ggplot(copepods, aes(temp_c, length_um)) +
    geom_point()
# Negative relationship between temperature and length
```

### Fit the model

Use the `lm()` to fit a model. Specify the relationship between repsonse and predictor with a _formula_.

```{r}
copepod_lm <- lm(length_um ~ temp_c, data = copepods)
```
Done!

## Interpret the model

Inspect the coefficients using `summary()`.

```{r}
summary(copepod_lm)
```

Use `sigma()` to ge the model estimate of sigma.

```{r}
sigma(copepod_lm)
```

When simulating data froma. linear regression model:

1. Choose our parameters (betas, sigma, n)
2. Simulate the data (predictor, expected, response)
3. Interpret the model (summary(), sigma())
